info.name: Inventory Manager — Firestore REST
info.description:
Exercises every Firestore collection the InventoryManager app reads/writes via the Firestore REST API.

## Auth
Every request needs a Firebase ID token in `Authorization: Bearer {{idToken}}`. Run **Setup → Get ID Token** first; it stores `idToken` in collection variables.

## Order to run
1. Setup → Get ID Token
2. Inventory Units (CRUD)
3. Inventory Aggregates
4. Sales
5. Suppliers
6. Scenarios 1–6 (each scenario is sequential — run requests top-to-bottom inside the folder).

## Variables
- `baseUrl` — Firestore REST documents root
- `authUrl` — Firebase Auth REST root
- `projectId`, `apiKey` — from `.env`
- `email`, `password` — admin credentials
- `idToken` — populated by Setup
- `imei`, `saleId`, `aggregateId`, `supplierId`, `shsUnitId` — populated by Scenario flows

## Soft-delete pattern
Returns NEVER hard-delete. `inventoryUnits/{imei}` is patched with `status='returned' + returnType='returned_to_supplier'` and the linked `sales/{saleId}` doc is patched with `voidedAt + voidReason`. The Sell-side surfaces filter out voided sales at runtime.

item.name: A. Setup
item.description: Run **Get ID Token** first — it exchanges email/password for a Firebase ID token and stores it as `idToken` for every other request.

request.description: POST email/password to Firebase Auth REST. Stores `idToken` + `localId` in collection variables. All subsequent Firestore calls use `Authorization: Bearer {{idToken}}`.

item.name: B. Inventory Units (CRUD)
item.description: Exercises `inventoryUnits` — keyed by IMEI/serial. Doc body uses Firestore's typed REST format (`{ fields: { imei: { stringValue: '…' } } }`).

body.raw:
{
  "fields": {
    "imei":            { "stringValue":  "{{imei}}" },
    "model":           { "stringValue":  "iPhone 15 Pro Max 256GB" },
    "brand":           { "stringValue":  "Apple" },
    "category":        { "stringValue":  "iPhone" },
    "colour":          { "stringValue":  "Natural Titanium" },
    "storage":         { "stringValue":  "256GB" },
    "grade":           { "stringValue":  "A" },
    "buyPrice":        { "integerValue": "850" },
    "dateIn":          { "stringValue":  "2026-05-17" },
    "supplierId":      { "stringValue":  "{{supplierId}}" },
    "supplierName":    { "stringValue":  "Demo Supplier" },
    "status":          { "stringValue":  "available" },
    "statusRaw":       { "stringValue":  "Office Stock" },
    "stockLocation":   { "stringValue":  "office" },
    "flags":           { "arrayValue": { "values": [] } },
    "notes":           { "stringValue":  "Created from Postman" },
    "platformListed":  { "booleanValue": false },
    "listingSites":    { "arrayValue": { "values": [] } },
    "ownerId":         { "stringValue":  "shared" },
    "createdAt":       { "timestampValue": "2026-05-17T09:00:00Z" }
  }
}

request.description: PATCH creates-or-updates the doc at `inventoryUnits/{imei}`. Firestore REST PATCH is an upsert.
`updateMask.fieldPaths` repeats once per field — only those fields are touched; everything else is preserved.
Hard delete. Returns and supplier-returns should use soft-delete (status='returned') instead — only use this for true cleanup.
POST /documents:runQuery — returns an array of `{ document: { name, fields } }` envelopes.

item.name: C. Inventory Aggregates
item.description: `inventoryAggregates` — model+supplier roll-up rows. Free-text quantity (`quantityText='SHS'`), compound colour breakdown (`coloursMap`).

item.name: D. Sales
item.description: `sales` — composite doc id `${marketplace}__${orderNumber}` for natural dedupe on re-import. Stored derived financial fields are computed by `calcSaleFinancials` in the client.

request.description: Voiding is a PATCH with updateMask — the doc stays in the collection for audit, but every Sell-side surface filters voided rows out of revenue / GP / Avg GP%.

item.name: F2. Scenario — Add SHS aggregate + receive
item.description: Create an SHS aggregate (quantityText='SHS', coloursMap of 4), then write one inventoryUnit per scanned IMEI and decrement the aggregate.

name: F3. Scenario — Sell + verify
description: Write a sale (composite id EBAY__order), flip the unit to status='sold', then GET the unit and assert.

name: F4. Scenario — Return to inventory + void sale
description: Flip the unit back to available with returnType='returned_to_inventory', mark the linked sale voided, then verify both.

name: 3. GET sales/{saleId} — assert voidedAt is set
4. GET inventoryUnits/{imei} — assert status='available' + returnType set
F5. Scenario — Return to supplier (soft delete)
description: Soft-delete policy: PATCH unit with status='returned' + returnType='returned_to_supplier'. Doc is preserved (no hard DELETE). Linked sale is voided.

item.name: 1. Seed a fresh sold unit + sale (so we have something to return)
3. PATCH inventoryUnits/{imei} → status='returned' + returnType='returned_to_supplier' (NO hard delete)

name: 5. GET inventoryUnits/{imei} — assert status='returned' AND doc still exists

exec: pm.test('Status 200 (doc still exists — soft delete)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

name: F6. Scenario — Sell SHS unit requires IMEI
description: An SHS placeholder unit has a synthetic id (e.g. `shs_iphone_15_demo_1`) and no IMEI. We backfill the IMEI first, then record the sale; finally we verify the unit has imei + status='sold'.
